body.statement: On \(\mathcal R_q\), computing \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions. Unless \(\mathrm{RP}=\mathrm{NP}\), no FPRAS exists even on matrices \(W_G\) obtained from graphs of maximum degree six. In contrast, \(N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W)=\operatorname{per}(\mathbf 1\{W\neq0\})\) has an FPRAS. Membership in \(\#\mathrm P\) is witnessed by a permutation and verified exactly by rational normalization followed by the Lyapunov certificate \(H-B_\pi^{\mathsf T}HB_\pi=I_q\) with \(H\succ0\).
body.justification: The result separates an approximable matching orbit from the causally relevant stability-filtered suborbit on the same normalized-assignment representation.
body.gap: Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda cover the unfiltered permanent, while Sly covers independent sets; the missing theorem is the one-call rational causal realization linking them.
body.consumer: It tells the matching-frequency sampler of Sharifian et al. that its permanent guarantee cannot be inherited after imposing equilibrium stability.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove membership in \(\#\mathrm P\) with the verifier stated in the theorem. Extend the promised function to all binary rational matrices by returning zero when the input is malformed or fails membership in \(\mathcal R_q\). Unit diagonal, rational encoding, and invertibility are decidable by exact rational arithmetic. Schur stability is also exactly decidable in polynomial time as follows.

For a rational matrix \(C\), solve the rational linear system
\[
 H-C^{\mathsf T}HC=I_q. \tag{3}
\]
If \(\rho(C)<1\), the convergent series
\[
 H=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(C^k)^{\mathsf T}C^k
\]
solves (3) and is positive definite. It is the unique solution because the homogeneous equation iterates to
\(H=(C^k)^{\mathsf T}HC^k\to0\). Conversely, if (3) has a positive-definite solution and \(Cv=\lambda v\) for a nonzero complex eigenvector, then
\[
 (1-|\lambda|^2)v^*Hv=v^*v>0,
\]
so \(|\lambda|<1\). Hence \(\rho(C)<1\). If the coefficient operator in (3) is singular, \(C\) cannot be stable, because stability gave uniqueness. Thus solving (3), checking symmetry, and applying exact positive-definiteness tests decides stability.

The system has dimension \(q^2\). Fraction-free elimination produces its unique rational solution, when it exists, with polynomially many bits by the determinant bound for an integer clearing of the denominators; exact \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) elimination or the leading-principal-minor criterion decides positive definiteness with polynomial bit complexity. This also decides the stable-reference promise in \(\mathcal R_q\).

Now guess a canonical encoding of a permutation \(\pi\). Verify that it is a bijection, check each rational denominator \(d_{\pi,i}\neq0\), construct \(B_\pi\) by the normalized-candidate definition, and apply (3) with \(C=B_\pi\). All arithmetic has polynomial bit complexity because normalization performs only rational division on input entries. Exactly one witness is accepted for each member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\), and no other witness is accepted. Therefore the extended count, and hence its restriction to \(\mathcal R_q\), belongs to \(\#\mathrm P\).

For hardness, the stable-orbit realization theorem is a deterministic polynomial-time map from a simple graph \(G\) to a matrix \(W_G\in\mathcal R_{3n}\), and it gives the exact equality
\[
 N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_G)=|\mathcal I(G)|. \tag{4}
\]
The independent-set counting lemma is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions. Equation (4) is a single, count-preserving oracle call, so computing \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}\) on \(\mathcal R_q\) is \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard under those reductions. Together with membership, this proves \(\#\mathrm P\)-completeness.

If an FPRAS existed on the images \(W_G\) of graphs of maximum degree six, applying it after the same map and using (4) would preserve both relative error and success probability, yielding an FPRAS for independent-set counting on maximum-degree-six graphs. This contradicts the cited degree-six inapproximability theorem unless \(\mathrm{RP}=\mathrm{NP}\). There is no subtraction, interpolation, or approximation-sensitive postprocessing in this transfer.

Finally define the zero-one support matrix
\[
 A(W)_{ri}=\mathbf1\{W_{ri}\neq0\}.
\]
By the admissible-orbit definition, a permutation \(\pi\) is admissible exactly when
\(\prod_iA(W)_{\pi(i),i}=1\). Therefore
\[
 N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W)
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_q}\prod_{i=1}^qA(W)_{\pi(i),i}
 =\operatorname{per}(A(W)).
\]
The support matrix is nonnegative, so the cited permanent theorem supplies an FPRAS. This proves the claimed separation between the unfiltered assignment orbit and its Schur-stable suborbit.
